rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

WITH customer_monthly_transaction_sums AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS month_total_amount
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY
  ct.customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER),
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)
HAVING SUM(ct.txn_amount) IS NOT NULL
),
customer_transaction_rows AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD if already in that form; otherwise pass through raw string
  txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
    WHEN txn_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE -txn_amount
  END AS txn_amount_signed,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
)
SELECT
  m.customer_id,
  m.year,
  m.month,
  printf('%04d-%02d-01', m.year, m.month) AS month_start_date,
  date(printf('%04d-%02d-01', m.year, m.month), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  closing_balance AS closing_balance,
  COALESCE(closing_balance - LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY m.customer_id ORDER BY m.year, m.month), closing_balance) AS monthly_change,
  closing_balance AS cumulative_balance
FROM (
  -- expand each customer's month span into one row per month
  WITH customer_ranges AS (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MIN(substr(txn_date, 1, 7)) AS min_ym,
      MAX(substr(txn_date, 1, 7)) AS max_ym
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ),
  months_expanded AS (
    SELECT
      cr.customer_id,
      CAST(substr(cr.min_ym,1,4) AS INTEGER) AS year,
      CAST(substr(cr.min_ym,6,2) AS INTEGER) AS month,
      cr.max_ym
    FROM customer_ranges cr
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
      me.customer_id,
      CASE WHEN me.month = 12 THEN me.year + 1 ELSE me.year END,
      CASE WHEN me.month = 12 THEN 1 ELSE me.month + 1 END,
      me.max_ym
    FROM months_expanded me
    WHERE printf('%04d-%02d', me.year, me.month) < me.max_ym
  ),
  months_distinct AS (
    SELECT customer_id, year, month FROM months_expanded
  ),
  -- attach monthly transaction sums (may be null -> treated as 0)
  month_with_amounts AS (
    SELECT
      md.customer_id,
      md.year,
      md.month,
      COALESCE(cmts.month_total_amount, 0.0) AS month_total_amount
    FROM months_distinct md
    LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_transaction_sums cmts
      ON cmts.customer_id = md.customer_id
     AND cmts.year = md.year
     AND cmts.month = md.month
  ),
  -- compute cumulative closing balance per customer by month
  closing AS (
    SELECT
      mwa.customer_id,
      mwa.year,
      mwa.month,
      SUM(mwa.month_total_amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY mwa.customer_id
        ORDER BY mwa.year, mwa.month
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) AS closing_balance
    FROM month_with_amounts mwa
  )
  SELECT customer_id, year, month, closing_balance FROM closing
) m
ORDER BY m.customer_id ASC, m.year ASC, m.month ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages

WITH all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
months AS (
  SELECT '01-2020' AS month_year, 1 AS month_num UNION ALL
  SELECT '02-2020', 2 UNION ALL
  SELECT '03-2020', 3 UNION ALL
  SELECT '04-2020', 4 UNION ALL
  SELECT '05-2020', 5 UNION ALL
  SELECT '06-2020', 6 UNION ALL
  SELECT '07-2020', 7 UNION ALL
  SELECT '08-2020', 8 UNION ALL
  SELECT '09-2020', 9 UNION ALL
  SELECT '10-2020', 10 UNION ALL
  SELECT '11-2020', 11 UNION ALL
  SELECT '12-2020', 12
),
customer_month_calendar_2020 AS (
  SELECT a.customer_id, m.month_year
  FROM all_customers a
  CROSS JOIN months m
  -- only keep customers that had at least one txn in 2020 per the original intent
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM customer_transactions ct
    WHERE ct.customer_id = a.customer_id
      AND substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) = '2020'
  )
),
customer_monthly_txn_sums AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    printf('%02d-2020', CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)) AS month_year,
    SUM(CASE WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END)
      - SUM(CASE WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) != 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customer_transactions ct
  WHERE substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) = '2020'
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_year
),
month_stats AS (
  SELECT
    cmc.month_year,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(cms.month_end_balance,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(cms.month_end_balance,0)) AS avg_balance
  FROM customer_month_calendar_2020 cmc
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_txn_sums cms
    ON cms.customer_id = cmc.customer_id
    AND cms.month_year = cmc.month_year
  GROUP BY cmc.month_year
)
SELECT
  high.month_year AS high_month,
  high.positive_count AS high_month_positive_customer_count,
  high.avg_balance AS high_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  low.month_year AS low_month,
  low.positive_count AS low_month_positive_customer_count,
  low.avg_balance AS low_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  (high.avg_balance - low.avg_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (SELECT month_year, positive_count, avg_balance
   FROM month_stats
   ORDER BY positive_count DESC, month_year ASC
   LIMIT 1) high,
  (SELECT month_year, positive_count, avg_balance
   FROM month_stats
   ORDER BY positive_count ASC, month_year ASC
   LIMIT 1) low

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_txn_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
),
customer_monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    cf.customer_id AS customer_id,
    date(substr(cf.txn_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(cf.txn_date,6,2) || '-01') AS month_start,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN cf.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN cf.txn_amount
        WHEN cf.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -cf.txn_amount
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS monthly_net
  FROM customer_txn_filtered cf
  GROUP BY cf.customer_id, month_start
),
customer_monthly_running AS (
  /* compute cumulative closing balance per customer per month */
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start,
    monthly_net,
    SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_net
),
customer_most_recent_and_prior AS (
  /* pick most recent month and the prior month's closing_balance for each customer */
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.month_start AS most_recent_month,
    m.closing_balance AS closing_balance_most_recent,
    p.closing_balance AS closing_balance_prior
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC) AS rn
    FROM customer_monthly_running
  ) m
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_running p
    ON m.customer_id = p.customer_id
    AND p.month_start = (
      SELECT month_start
      FROM customer_monthly_running cr2
      WHERE cr2.customer_id = m.customer_id
        AND cr2.month_start < m.month_start
      ORDER BY cr2.month_start DESC
      LIMIT 1
    )
  WHERE m.rn = 1
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5_percent,
  SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS num_customers_with_growth_gt_5,
  COUNT(*) AS total_customers_evaluated,
  (SELECT MAX(month_start) FROM customer_monthly_net) AS most_recent_month_reference
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    closing_balance_most_recent,
    closing_balance_prior,
    CASE
      WHEN closing_balance_prior IS NULL OR closing_balance_prior = 0 THEN closing_balance_most_recent * 100.0
      ELSE (closing_balance_most_recent - closing_balance_prior) / closing_balance_prior
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM customer_most_recent_and_prior
) final

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- parse txn_date and get min/max per customer
cust_ranges AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(min(txn_date)) AS min_date,
    date(max(txn_date)) AS max_date
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- generate all dates per customer by joining with recursive sequence
dates_per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    cr.customer_id,
    cr.min_date AS dt,
    cr.max_date
  FROM cust_ranges cr
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    dpc.customer_id,
    date(dpc.dt, '+1 day') AS dt,
    dpc.max_date
  FROM dates_per_customer dpc
  WHERE dpc.dt < dpc.max_date
),
-- sum transactions per customer per day (signed amounts assumed in txn_amount; if txn_type implies sign, adjust here)
daily_txn AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS dt,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, date(txn_date)
),
-- left join generated dates to daily_txn to get 0 when no txn that day
daily_amounts_filled AS (
  SELECT
    dpc.customer_id,
    dpc.dt,
    IFNULL(dt_sum.daily_amount, 0) AS daily_amount
  FROM dates_per_customer dpc
  LEFT JOIN daily_txn dt_sum
    ON dpc.customer_id = dt_sum.customer_id
   AND dpc.dt = dt_sum.dt
),
-- compute running balance per customer by date; use recursive CTE ordered by date per customer
running_balances AS (
  -- anchor: first date per customer
  SELECT
    daf.customer_id,
    daf.dt,
    -- balance is daily_amount on first day (can be negative; will clamp later)
    daf.daily_amount AS balance
  FROM daily_amounts_filled daf
  WHERE daf.dt = (
    SELECT MIN(dt) FROM daily_amounts_filled d2 WHERE d2.customer_id = daf.customer_id
  )

  UNION ALL

  -- recursive step: next date for same customer
  SELECT
    daf.customer_id,
    daf.dt,
    -- previous balance + today's amount
    (rb.balance + daf.daily_amount) AS balance
  FROM running_balances rb
  JOIN daily_amounts_filled daf
    ON daf.customer_id = rb.customer_id
   AND daf.dt = date(rb.dt, '+1 day')
),
-- clamp negative balances to zero
running_balances_clamped AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    dt,
    CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END AS balance
  FROM running_balances
),
-- extract month and compute per-customer per-month max daily balance
cust_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', dt) AS month,
    MAX(balance) AS max_balance
  FROM running_balances_clamped
  GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', dt)
)
-- final: sum per-customer monthly maxima across customers, ordered by month
SELECT
  month AS month,
  SUM(max_balance) AS monthly_total_max_balances
FROM cust_month_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC
